gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the rear channel of a sub-$250 "4K+4K" camera records beyond its pixel count: DashCamTalk lists the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K rear at 3840×2160, 30 fps, 24 Mbps with no HDR, which is fewer bits per pixel (0.10) than the VIOFO A229 Pro's 2K rear (0.23, 25 Mbps with HDR).
standout_why: Compared against productbible (front-and-rear), roadgearlab, the-gadgeteer, digitalcameraworld and knowledgelib; caranddriver.com could not be fetched. Rivals hold parts: roadgearlab relays DashCamTalk bitrates for the A229 Pro (57 + 25 Mbps) and 70mai A810S (29 + 10 Mbps) and explains native versus interpolated 4K by sensor; knowledgelib gives the Miofive S1 Ultra as 3840×2160 at 30 fps front and 25 fps rear, with the rear shipped set to 1440p; productbible names sensors; the-gadgeteer has the ROVE R2-4K Dual (non-Pro) at 25 fps. None covers the Vantrue S1 Pro Max or Redtiger F77, none puts rear resolution, fps, sensor megapixels, HDR and bitrate side by side for the dual-4K cameras under $250, and none says whether quoted frame rates hold with both cameras recording. Held at 2, not 3, because the rear-HDR and bitrate figures rest on one DashCamTalk spec table that contradicts itself elsewhere, and Vantrue's own page and manual could not be read.
decides: It splits the question in two. If "4K front and rear" means 3840×2160 on both cameras, the candidate under $250 is the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K (partner store, $239.99 in the brief's 2026-11-21 table, no record yet; I could not re-read it, vantrue.com returned HTTP 429): DashCamTalk lists an 8 MP IMX678 at each end at 30 fps, with the footnote that the rear has no HDR and 24 Mbps. If the shopper wants the most usable rear evidence, a 4K + 2K camera with HDR on both channels remains the pick on paper (VIOFO A229 Pro 2CH; among ours the DDPAI N5 Pro or Z90 Pro, whose per-channel figures I could not read). Budget check for rival rows: the makers' US stores list the VIOFO A229 Pro 2CH and the ROVE R2-4K Dual Pro at $349.99 each on 2026-11-21, so both sit under $250 only at the Amazon prices rivals quote ($219.99 and about $206), which I could not verify because Amazon search returned nothing. The Redtiger F77 ($189.99) is the other dual-IMX678 under budget, but its rear fps and HDR are unread.
